reads_as: a Floyd's-cycle Python snippet on dark navy diagonally split against a wide-eyed creator throwing an anime fighting pose with manga speed-lines
layout_map: Frame split by a diagonal seam running top-center (~x640,y0) down to lower-left (~x440,y720). LEFT wedge is a dark-navy code editor: monospaced Python (mint/blue/white syntax) with line numbers 22-37 in the gutter, the function `def findDuplicate(nums):` starting cell ~x60,y100, body filling the wedge to bottom-left. RIGHT wedge is a real photo on a white/grey room: the creator from chest up, head cells 8-11 (~x900,y230), dark intense downward stare, mouth set, one gloved hand raised flat near the face (~x1130,y380) in a martial pose. White radial manga speed-lines burst from a point behind his head across both wedges, densest top-right and lower-left. No headline text, no badge; the code IS the left-half graphic.
why_it_works: the literal algorithm screenshot promises real substance while the anime pose plus speed-lines injects energy and comedy, so the click feels both educational and fun
mimic_for: a beat where we show real code or an algorithm but want the energy of a dramatic reveal — split our editor capture against a reacting face with burst lines
title: If Programming Was An Anime

reads_as: a pensive creator chewing a pen behind a floating layer of hand-drawn chalk-green equations and geometry, like he's thinking through hard math
layout_map: Full-bleed muted indoor photo. The creator fills the right-center, head cells 4-8 (~x780,y130) with a long-hair beard, pen tip held to his lips (~x780,y350), forearm crossed across lower frame. A translucent overlay of chalk-green (low-opacity white-green) hand-drawn math floats over the WHOLE frame: a geometric diamond/triangle diagram top-left (cells 1-3), scattered equations like `x=a/E`, fractions and `mc^2`-style terms top-right (cells 4-6, ~x1080,y90), sine curves and `(ln/u)` bottom-left (~x80,y560), and `(m-4)(m)` bottom-right (~x1100,y620). The equations read as a transparent glass blackboard sitting in front of him. No solid headline text, no badge.
why_it_works: the floating equation glass instantly signals 'serious math' while the contemplative chew-the-pen face frames it as a struggle the viewer shares, selling a dry topic as relatable
mimic_for: a conceptual or math-heavy beat where we want a thinking-face still wrapped in a translucent layer of the actual formulas or diagram the video unpacks
title: why you NEED math for programming

reads_as: a deadpan presenter in an Apple-keynote black void cradling a window blind like a precious product, with the white Apple logo floating top-right
layout_map: Near-black studio void with a soft vertical key-light glow behind the subject (center column, brightest cells 2-7). The creator stands center, glasses + black turtleneck (Jobs-coded), head cells 5-6 (~x690,y130), deadpan straight-to-camera. His hands present a white horizontal window-blind held vertically on the LEFT third, the blind object filling cells 8-13 (~x230,y400) like a hero gadget under spotlight. A large solid-white Apple logo sits top-right, cells 7-8 (~x1080,y150), ~12% frame height. No headline text — the visual parody (turtleneck + void + Apple mark + mundane object) carries it.
why_it_works: borrowing Apple's instantly-recognized keynote staging and logo makes an absurd object read as a 'premium product launch', and the void plus deadpan face sells the joke without any words
mimic_for: a satirical or hype beat where we present a mundane tech thing as a faux product launch — black void, presenter, a borrowed brand mark, and the object spotlit center
title: if Apple made window blinds...

reads_as: a wary beanie-wearing guy leaning on a propped shotgun, with a yellow handwritten-feel question 'how do you even work here?' across the lower frame
layout_map: Full-bleed handheld photo of a bright apartment. The creator fills right-center, head cells 5-7 (~x650,y130), black beanie, raised eyebrows, mouth slightly open in a wary/confused look, body in a black hoodie angled toward camera. A black shotgun barrel juts in from the LEFT edge resting under his arm (~x100,y360 → x430,y310). Two-line yellow caption (rounded bold sans, ~64px, black-edge contrast) sits lower-right: 'how do you even' baseline ~y490 (cells 8-11, ~x650), 'work here?' baseline ~y560 below it. Cluttered shelf with figurines fills the right edge background.
why_it_works: the prop plus a startled face creates instant 'what is going on here' tension, and the casual lowercase yellow question reads like overheard dialogue that demands the click to resolve
mimic_for: a comedic or confrontational hook beat where a startled face plus a short lowercase overheard-question caption (yellow on the lower frame) poses the video's premise
title: when you rob a big tech company, but the employees are...

reads_as: a deadpan junior dev seated in an open-plan tech office with a clean white role label captioning him along the bottom edge
layout_map: Full-bleed photo of a bright industrial open-plan office (Aeron chairs, exposed ceiling, a coder visible far right). The creator sits center-frame from chest up, head cells 5-7 (~x540,y130), maroon cap + green field jacket over a hoodie, flat unimpressed straight-to-camera stare, hands resting on a desk near the lower edge. A white bold sans caption 'Junior Engineer - SF Office' runs along the bottom-left edge, baseline ~y505 (cells 9-12, ~x40), ~46px, slight drop-shadow for legibility against the desk. No accent color, no badge — the label and deadpan face are the whole composition.
why_it_works: the plain factual role label plus a deadpan corporate stare sets up a relatable workplace persona, inviting the viewer to recognize the type and click to see them in action
mimic_for: a persona or role-archetype beat where we caption a deadpan seated face with a simple white role/title label along the bottom to set up a workplace character
title: how we write/review code in big tech companies

reads_as: A guy in a purple tee and headband slumps lazily in an office chair inside a sunlit high-rise home office with a city skyline behind him.
layout_map: No headline text, no badge — pure candid scene. Subject seated in office chair right-of-center, body in cells 7,11 and head ~x780,y230 (cell 7 lower edge); purple shirt + bright-yellow shorts are the color anchor, legs sprawling into cell 11 ~x680,y480. White/navy ergonomic chair fills cells 11,12,15,16. Environment fills the frame left-to-right: floor-to-ceiling window with hazy city skyline across the top band (cells 1-8, y0-200) with a soft sun-bloom glow upper-center ~x560,y90; desk with dual dark monitors + boom mic occupying left third, mic ~x90,y260 (cell 5), monitors cells 5-6; patterned area rug across the bottom (cells 13-16); dark bookshelf along far-right edge cells 8,12. Eye-level wide shot, no overlays.
why_it_works: The relatable slouched, eyes-half-closed body language paired with an aspirational skyline-view home office creates an instant "this is the chill WFH day I want" mood that stops the scroll with zero text.
mimic_for: a relaxed day-in-the-life / work-from-home lifestyle intro beat where the candid scene itself is the hook
title: a day in the life of an engineer working from home

reads_as: A young programmer grips his own head with both hands in stressed exasperation, filling the frame against a blurred office desk-setup, with no text at all.
layout_map: Single full-bleed face dominating center, cells 6,7,10,11; head/hairline tops at ~y20, eyes ~y90, chin ~y150, face center ~x160,y100; both hands raised gripping the sides of his head — left hand cells 5-6 ~x110,y50, right hand cells 7-8 ~x210,y50; pale gray turtleneck collar lower-center cells 10-11 ~y150; blurred office background — monitors/desk-setup upper-right cell 8 ~x270,y40, blurred room left cells 1,5 ~x40,y60; no headline, no badge, no accent graphics.
why_it_works: The pure no-text, head-in-hands stress expression filling the entire frame reads as instant relatable frustration, forcing the viewer to lean on the title for the punchline.
mimic_for: A relatable pain/frustration beat — the moment a developer is overwhelmed or exasperated by a situation.
title: how programmers attend meetings at big tech companies

reads_as: A coder turns from a wall of interview-prep monitors to face the camera with a skeptical, worried look, caught mid-thought.
layout_map: No text overlay. Subject (Joma) seated right, body in black sweater turned over-the-shoulder toward camera; head cells 4,8 center ~x830,y230, hands clasped at chin cells 11,12 ~x720,y400; subject occupies right ~40% (cells 4,8,12,16). Hero context = curved ultrawide monitor full of code plus a top diagram monitor (Google PM interview sketch-notes) filling left-center cells 1-3,5-7,9-11; MacBook lid bottom-center cells 13-15; RODE shotgun mic top-center cell 4 ~x740,y60; blown-out window light upper-right and warm lemons/orange decor far-right edge cell 16. mimic_for: a candid first-person confession or reality-check about the grind behind a skill or career move
title: how programmers overprepare for job interviews

reads_as: A programmer in a black cap and face mask sits typing at a laptop in an empty office, with no text at all.
layout_map: No headline text anywhere. Masked figure centered-upper: head + black cap cells 2-3 center ~x190,y55, torso fills cells 6-7,10-11 down to ~y360; black face mask covers nose/mouth ~x190,y90 (the pandemic tell). title: how coronavirus affects programmers in big tech companies

mimic_for: a deadpan character-driven skit beat that mock-awards a "best/worst [role]" title
title: If American Psycho were about Programmers

title: interviewing at a startup be like... (ft. Steven He)

reads_as: A strained, open-mouthed coder sits centered amid a wall of glowing code monitors with a giant white "10 Years of Coding" headline running across the bottom.
layout_map: Shocked open-mouth face dead-center, cells 6,7,10,11, head ~x640,y320, ~30% frame height, body in light grey tee; full-bleed environment of stacked glowing code/visual monitors fills all corners behind him (cells 1-4 top, 9-12 mid-sides); bottom white headline "10 Years of Coding" Inter-700 mixed-case, cells 13-16, spanning full width, baseline ~y690, cap-height ~70px, left edge ~x10; no badge, no number stat, no accent color.

mimic_for: A retrospective or "everything I learned" beat summarizing a long stretch of work in one overwhelmed reaction.
title: 10 years of coding in 13 minutes

mimic_for: a dramatized "coding under pressure" or programming-as-battle beat pitting raw code against an intensely-focused reaction face
title: If Programming Was An Anime 2

title: I Built a Trading Bot to let Subscribers Trade $25,000 on Twitch

title: What REALLY is Data Science? Told by a Data Scientist

title: Coding a whole web app ONLY using my Phone.
